text: I want my assistant to remember that I am vegetarian, without any company holding that fact for me.
So the memory gets a key that only my passkey can make. One touch, and the vault is open.
Now I tell Pip two things that should last. I'm vegetarian. I fly out of B L R.
cap: Now I tell Pip two things that should last. I'm vegetarian. I fly out of BLR.

text: The model picks out each fact with a tool call. Then the browser seals it, at epoch one.
The second fact goes the same way. Three things have to hold: the key is mine, an app's access is a grant, and a revoke really ends it.
What gets stored is ciphertext. No fact in the clear, anywhere outside this tab.
Fern is a second assistant, from a different app, with its own key. It sees nothing yet.
Connect asks Pip for access, and Pip asks me. A grant is a transaction, so the owner needs gas, and the page says exactly how much is missing.
I send a little M O N to that address, then allow.
cap: I send a little MON to that address, then allow.

text: One transaction on Monad records a wrapped key for Fern. That hash is real, and Fern rebuilds the grant from it alone.
Only two things live on chain: the grant, and the epoch number.
Fern never touched my passkey. A key of its own and the grant are all it has.
Fern opens both memories with its own key. Now I ask it to plan my weekend.
It plans around vegetarian food and a flight out of Bengaluru. Two of two memories read.
It never asks what I eat or where I fly from.
Now I change my mind. Revoke is one more transaction. The folder moves to epoch two, and the browser seals every memory again under the new key.
That reseal is why the old grant is dead. The key Fern holds belongs to epoch one, and nothing is sealed there any more.
Fern still holds its old grant. I ask again, and every memory comes back grant revoked.
cap: Fern still holds its old grant. I ask again, and every memory comes back GRANT_REVOKED.

text: The plan comes back generic, with none of my facts. The registry did that, not a promise from Fern.
Straight from the chain: the grant and the revoke both succeeded, and the folder's epoch went from one to two.
cap: Straight from the chain: the grant and the revoke both succeeded, and the folder's epoch went from one to two.

text: Two transactions, and nothing in between that I have to trust.
Developers get the same thing with npm install satchel S D K.
cap: Developers get the same thing with npm install satchel-sdk.

text: One passkey prompt, a sealed record, a value that comes back. The code on the page is the code that runs.
Seal, grant, revoke. Three calls against the same registry.
